‍


Coding agents can now run for days.


The longer they run, the less they remember.


As an agent works for hours or days, its context gets repeatedly compressed, potentially losing important details along the way.


Shalin Patel, Co-Founder & CEO of OpenCrawl, found that preserving the entire session transcript and making it searchable led to fewer turns, faster execution and lower costs.


OpenCrawl reports outperforming competing published scores on BEAM, a memory benchmark, across histories ranging from 100,000 to 10 million tokens.


But memory is only part of the problem. Coordination is another.


Agents running in separate cloud environments typically don't share transcripts or context. When a temporary sandbox shuts down, locally stored session history can disappear with it.


The same fragmentation exists across teams.


One engineer uses Claude Code, another uses Codex, and a third uses Conductor. Their agents operate independently, even when they're working toward the same objective.


OpenCrawl connects these agents through a shared memory layer and message board, allowing them to search previous sessions, communicate and coordinate their work.


One early customer, a GTM platform, extended OpenCrawl beyond its software engineers to its growth team.


Previously, one agent might restructure pricing around product-led growth while another redesigned the landing page exclusively for enterprise customers.


After implementing OpenCrawl, the team reported greater consistency without having to repeatedly remind its agents of the company's strategy.


The open-source approach also serves two purposes: encouraging developers to build on top of OpenCrawl and holding the company accountable for the quality of its code and benchmarks.


In the two weeks leading up to our conversation, the YC-backed startup went from zero to 22 paying users.


Shalin predicts the developer population could grow at least fivefold by 2040 as AI makes software development accessible to more people.


As more people build with more agents across more platforms, the need for shared memory and coordination will only grow.


That's the future OpenCrawl is building toward: multiplayer for your coding agents.
